findings: The route accepts one Senate/House selector only, sends no-store responses, and never accepts client-selected lock paths or hashes. The fixed server publication config chooses exact lock and ledger subject/publication/admission pins. The artifact store rehashes bytes, rejects unsafe paths and symlinks, verifies independent admissions, and uses only the explicit complete ledger head.

Missing publication config is a distinct lock_not_configured state. Malformed config, corrupt lock/ledger pins, and scoring failures become unavailable without source paths or a fabricated no-lock claim. A selected empty ledger yields pending rows and no grade. Corrected revision tests show a new head and source revision, not timestamp-based selection.

The result view whitelists source metadata and hash provenance, not raw source text. Called/provisional observations can be visible while losses remain null under certified-minimum protocols. Partial scores are labeled as available-row diagnostics; an overall letter is exposed only when the locked grader reports complete eligible cohorts.

The excluded Senate display race remains in the forecast/result table with display_only diagnostics but no rubric loss and outside-primary-grade labeling. Scored denominator stays the declared cohort. Current issued House scoring requires 435 party winners, 412 supported named pairs and 23 predeclared pair exclusions; House native target/law IDs remain explicitly null. Group winners are shown separately from candidate-pair margins.

The UI compares the current result SHA with the locked model SHA and identifies a different edition. Refresh follows the server-selected head on focus/visibility or the visible 60-second interval; stale or failed refresh clears the prior evaluation view. Per-race cards distinguish reported locked races from unreported ones.

limits: The frozen-at timestamp is checked to follow both forecast issue times, but this code alone cannot prove an external pre-result timestamp; independent lock admission and witnessed release evidence remain required. Source URLs and permission still depend on the separately admitted source/result policy. The tests use invented election observations; no real result or public evaluation was claimed.
